covers: Monday 2 November 2026 from the Asian session to the JSE afternoon (no US session since Friday's close)
headline: WTI briefly dips below $100 as Iran talks lift hopes; SA factory PMI improves to 49.6 but stays in contraction; rand steady near R16.70
summary: South Africa's Absa manufacturing PMI rose to 49.6 in October from a revised 48.7 in September, a second monthly gain but still below the 50 line that separates growth from contraction (Absa via IT-Online and Reuters, 2 Nov), while the rand held steady at about R16.70 per dollar (FNB via DMarketForces, 2 Nov). In the US, futures were up about 0.4% ahead of ISM manufacturing at 16:00 SAST and Apple and Palantir results tonight (Trading Economics via TradingView; TradingKey, 2 Nov). US WTI crude briefly traded below $100 (range $99.80–$102.75) and Brent between $108.89 and $112.41 by 10:14 GMT after Iran's negotiators left Doha with a draft proposal circulating (Newsquawk, 2 Nov) — a deal would ease oil and help the rand, but nothing is agreed and the post-midterm risk of renewed US strikes remains.

items.title: US WTI crude briefly dips below $100 a barrel as Iran diplomacy hopes build; silver back above $50
items.summary: By 10:14 GMT (12:14 SAST) on Monday 2 November, WTI December futures had traded between $99.80 and $102.75 a barrel, briefly dipping below $100, against Friday's $102.43–$104.99 range; Brent January traded between $108.89 and $112.41 (Friday: $111.03–$114.29). Sources said Iran's negotiators left Doha on Sunday not because of difficulties, that a draft proposal was circulated for feedback and a follow-up meeting is possible; Iran's foreign ministry spokesperson Baghaei called the shortened two-day plan a sign of goodwill and said the US must decide. Major OPEC+ producers kept December quotas unchanged, limiting the fall. Spot gold traded $3,891–$3,919 an ounce and spot silver reclaimed $50 (range $49.11–$50.55); LME copper rose 1.0% (Newsquawk, 2 Nov 2026). Nothing is agreed yet.

items.title: Oil deepens its fall to about 3.7% (Brent $109.23, WTI near $100) as Iranian negotiators leave Doha
items.summary: By 09:00 GMT (11:00 SAST) on Monday 2 November Brent crude futures were down $4.20, or 3.7%, at $109.23 a barrel, and US WTI traded at $100.14, down $3.98 or 3.8%, on hopes that talks between Iranian and Qatari officials could ease Middle East supply disruptions. Iranian negotiators left the Doha talks on Sunday; an official briefed on the meeting said this was not because of difficulties in the negotiations. Analysts also pointed to the lack of military escalation over the weekend (Reuters report via PressNewsAgency/CNA, 2 Nov 2026). Nothing has been agreed yet. The rand held steady at about R16.70 per dollar (FNB) and gold rebounded to $3,905.21 an ounce (DMarketForces, 2 Nov 2026) — cheaper oil is a support for the rand and for SA fuel prices if it holds.
items.source: Reuters via PressNewsAgency, 2 Nov 2026; DMarketForces, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: Iran: a 'two-day plan' brokered by Qatar and Pakistan could reopen the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Speaking to Al Jazeera on Sunday, Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said Qatari and Pakistani mediators had reworked Iran's original seven-day plan and 'we have now reached a two-day plan': on day one 'America will implement a set of measures' and on day two the strait would reopen. The measures were not specified; security chief Mohsen Rezaei said the blockade would stay until conditions including 'releasing frozen assets' were met, and said the tone of a letter from US Vice President JD Vance had 'completely changed'. Trump said on Saturday the talks were 'going fine but you know they're not very reliable' (Arab News, 2 Nov 2026). This is the main driver behind Monday's oil fall; nothing has been agreed yet.

items.title: Earlier: Oil down about 3% (Brent near $110) on Iran–Qatar talks and reports Trump prefers more time for diplomacy
items.summary: By 05:27 GMT on Monday 2 November Brent January futures were down 3.3% at $109.70 a barrel and WTI down 3.5% at $100.48 (Investing.com, 2 Nov 2026), deepening an earlier 1.4% fall. Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araqchi called the talks with Qatar 'ongoing and progressing', and KCM Trade's Tim Waterer called the drop a 'technical pullback' after last week's gains, warning Brent could approach $120 if rhetoric escalates after Tuesday's US midterms (Reuters via Arab News, 2 Nov 2026). Citing an Axios report, Investing.com said Trump told Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu on Saturday he preferred to give diplomacy more time before deciding on renewed military action. OPEC+ kept December output targets unchanged. Cheaper oil helps the rand and SA fuel prices if it holds. Later on Monday Brent was about $110.00, down about 3.0% on the day and below Friday's level above $113; the four-year high of $116.72 was set on 23 October (Trading Economics, 2 Nov 2026).
items.source: Investing.com; Reuters via Arab News, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: Stock futures up about 0.4% after last week's tech sell-off
items.summary: Early on Monday S&P 500 and Nasdaq 100 futures were up about 0.4% and Dow futures 0.3%. Last week the Nasdaq Composite fell 2%, the Dow 0.85% and the S&P 500 0.57%, after weak tech results and worries about AI spending (Trading Economics via TradingView, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: Busy week: midterms Tuesday, October jobs report Friday, and Apple, Palantir, AMD and Qualcomm results
items.summary: Apple and Palantir report after the US close on Monday 2 November; AMD reports after the close on Tuesday 3 November, Qualcomm and Arm on Wednesday 4 November. ISM manufacturing is due Monday at 10:00 ET (16:00 SAST) and ISM services on Wednesday. The US midterm elections are on Tuesday 3 November, and the October employment report comes on Friday 6 November at 8:30 ET (14:30 SAST). The Fed's target range is 3.75%–4.00% (TradingKey, 2 Nov 2026). Reuters reported about an 80% chance of a December Fed hike (Tech Insider, Nov 2026).

items.title: Absa PMI improves to 49.6 in October, a second monthly gain, but factories are still contracting
items.summary: The seasonally adjusted Absa manufacturing PMI rose 0.9 points to 49.6 in October from a revised 48.7 in September, just below the 50-point line. All five headline components improved: business activity 48.6 (from 47.7), new sales orders 46.8 (45.4), employment 44.2 (42.8), inventories 50.4 (49.7) and supplier deliveries 58.1 (58.0). But the purchasing price index climbed to 73.7 from 71.1 and expected business conditions in six months fell to 51.7 from 55.3; the report said demand 'remains insufficient to support a sustained recovery' and 'the recovery remains fragile' (Absa PMI via IT-Online, 2 Nov 2026; Reuters via Club of Mozambique, 2 Nov 2026). Rising input costs are a watch point for SA inflation and the SARB.
items.source: IT-Online, 2 Nov 2026; Reuters via Club of Mozambique, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: Wednesday 4 November is a public holiday for the local government elections
items.summary: President Cyril Ramaphosa declared local government election day, 4 November, a public holiday under the Public Holidays Act by notice in the Government Gazette (BusinessTech). That makes this a four-day trading week for South Africa, with US results and the midterm outcome landing around the holiday.

items.title: Concor, the PIC-owned construction group, is in business rescue; more than 2,200 jobs at risk
items.summary: Concor's board found the business financially distressed and filed for business rescue on 6 October 2026, covering Concor Holdings, Concor (Pty) Ltd, Concor Construction and Concor Mining. The company is owned by the GEPF (81.25%) and UIF (18.75%), managed by the PIC, which cites liquidity and working-capital strain, legacy projects and guarantee calls after partner Murray & Roberts' 2024 rescue. Moneyweb reports more than 2,200 jobs at risk; Concor is a joint-venture partner on the R1.65 billion Msikaba bridge on the N2 Wild Coast road (Moneyweb, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: Rand slightly firmer near R16.69 on Monday, still close to its weakest since July
items.summary: USD/ZAR was at 16.6864 on Monday 2 November, down 0.13% on the day (rand firmer), after closing Friday at 16.7075. Trading Economics cites a firm dollar, weaker gold and PGM prices and high oil as the pressures, partly offset by a well-received Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement; September CPI was 4.5% (Trading Economics, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: Gold back near $3,900 after its worst October since 2008; platinum still falling
items.summary: At 01:01 GMT on Monday spot gold was up 0.6% at $3,900.05 an ounce and silver up 1.4% at $49.83, while platinum was down 3.4% at $1,434.65 and palladium down 2.6% at $980.35. Gold had fallen 3.7% to a one-year low in the prior session. Lower oil eased some inflation worries; the US dollar index was down 0.2% at 101.88 (Investing.com, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: Goldman Sachs lifts its December Brent forecast to $105 from $90
items.summary: Goldman raised its December forecasts to $105 for Brent (from $90) and $94 for WTI, and its 2027 averages to $88 for Brent (from $80) and $78 for WTI (from $73), citing supply risks from the Middle East and Russia–Ukraine and adding a 1 million barrel-a-day disruption allowance to its 2027 base case (investingLive, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: AAPL and PLTR report tonight; both rated HOLD by the LRC Stock Scanner
items.summary: Apple (HOLD, score 61) closed Friday at $344.63, down 1.2%, and Palantir (HOLD, score 72) at $184.11, down 6.3% (LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026). Both report after the US close on Monday 2 November (TradingKey, 2 Nov 2026). Results can move the scanner score; ratings are not changed by this brief.
items.source: LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026; TradingKey, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: AMD (Tuesday) and QCOM (Wednesday) report after Friday's chip sell-off
items.summary: AMD (HOLD, score 69) fell 10.9% to $504.80 on Friday and Qualcomm (HOLD, score 39) 11.1% to $164.79 in the Intel-led chip sell-off (LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026). AMD reports after the close on Tuesday 3 November and Qualcomm on Wednesday 4 November (TradingKey, 2 Nov 2026).
items.source: LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026; TradingKey, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: JSE gold and PGM miners closed Friday 5.6–6.4% lower; gold's Monday bounce is a first test
items.summary: On Friday 30 October Gold Fields fell 6.4% to R553.06, Sibanye-Stillwater 6.4% to R35.77, Harmony 6.3% to R245.58, AngloGold Ashanti 6.0% to R1,340.52 and Implats 5.6% to R163.91, while Sasol rose 1.2% to R289.45 on higher oil (LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026). Spot gold's 0.6% rise in Asia (Investing.com, 2 Nov) is the first sign for Monday's open; platinum is still down.
items.source: LRC Stock Scanner, 30 Oct 2026; Investing.com, 2 Nov 2026
